conclusion: Against a ten-mutant battery, tests/test_doors.py detects 5/10 door-breaking mutants: four on the fast tier (README naming a missing script, a script renamed on disk, and the two interactive_lab contract clauses) and one only on the slow tier (the ledger's own named mutant, a README-quoted command that exits non-zero). The five escapes share one cause — the guard reads only the docs/doors/README.md table and only for the regex scripts/[\w.]+\.py, so commands quoted inside door pages, and README rows naming no script at all (the certify and adopt doors), are outside its field of view entirely.
confidence: High for the catch/escape verdicts themselves: the null control passes both tiers, each verdict is a pytest process exit status, and the five escapes were also run simultaneously on one tree that stayed green on both tiers. Lower for the number 5/10 as a characterisation of the guard: ten mutants chosen by one reader of the source is a sample, not a census, and at least three further plausible misses (inline import(), an empty <title>, a second interactive_lab page) were named but not built.
